newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Congress reopens after a two-week recess to deliberate on the 476.2 billion peso budget bill and other vital measures before it adjourns again for the Christmas holiday, House speaker Jose de Venecia says. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- President Fidel Ramos vows adequate security and the "best possible kind of hosting" for delegates in the leaders' summit this month of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Operations of Philipine Airlines normalise following Saturday's signing of a memorandum between management and a striking employees' union. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The retail trade liberisation bill will not be approved by the Senate before the end of the year, Senate president Ernesto Maceda says, but he promises to approve the Intellectual Property Rights Code (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The country's three oil firms are requesting the Department of Finance to put off lifting the remaining 90-day foreign exchange cover until the full deregulation of the energy sector (BUSINESS DAILY)

- A squabble between PNOC Petrochemical Development Corp and Petrochemical Corp of Asia over the proposed $500-million naphtha cracker project heats up as both camps refuse to give in to each other's proposition (INQUIRER)
- The Central Bank reports a slight increase foreign debt stock from $37.78 billion last year to $37.87 billion as of the middle of the year (INQUIRER)
